children: HSBC raised its oil-price forecasts for this year and next, saying it expects the market to remain in deficit until around mid-2027. "The revision to our crude oil price forecasts reflects a permanent disruption of the Strait of Hormuz and a longer path back to market equilibrium, with a 'new normal' that does not revert to the pre-conflict situation," analysts at the bank say. HSBC now projects Brent at $95 a barrel in the fourth quarter and at $90 a barrel for 2026 as a whole. In 2027, Brent is seen at $85 a barrel. Hormuz flows are expected to recover only gradually, reaching 8 million barrels a day by year-end and 9.5 million barrels a day by mid-2027, compared with around 19 million-20 million barrels a day before the conflict. (giulia.petroni@wsj.com)
